structure: Woodham Ferrers junction (east of level crossing)
survey_description: Maldon branch diverged from the Southminster line immediately east of the level crossing; alignment now houses and property boundaries, plus a footpath north of Bancrofts Road
3-arched blue engineering brick bridge (bridge 833); cutting about 3 m below the field to the west; line preserved beneath the main arch
Line marked by a strip of woodland; footbridge at TQ824989 shown c.1897 not extant

structure: Church Lane bridge / Stow St Mary Halt
survey_description: Bridge of 3 segmental arches, blue engineering brick (bridge 836); halt platform was wooden sleepers; now a nature reserve; line in a woodland strip
Cutting gives way to an embankment; line preserved in a woodland strip
Track crossed over the lane on a blue engineering brick bridge; only the two abutments remain (approximate position: survey NGR has five digits)

structure: St Stephens Road bridge, Cold Norton
survey_description: Iron girder bridge with blue brick parapet (bridge 839); ground to the north raised about 3.5 m to form a front lawn
Three 25.5 ft segmental arches, blue engineering brick with dentilled decoration (bridge 840); cutting partly filled in to the north by about 3 m
Embankment bridge; only the blue engineering brick abutments remain
Girder and blue engineering brick bridge with blue brick copings; halt platform to the west of the track, north of the bridge, in a shallow cutting; access incline still extant in 2011

Tunnel under Spital Road, length disputed: the survey gives both 66 yards (60 m) and 21 m; a georeferenced trace of the covered/cutting extent favours something close to 66 yards, not 21 m (see docs/research/maldon_west_corrections.md) - treat both as unconfirmed. Blocked at both ends in 2011; south portal balustrade intact; north end possibly beneath the bypass
Brick arch and bowstring girder viaduct, 75 ft span, built 1889 (bridge 852), on an embankment; central span demolished 1965, piers 1989; replaced by a 1990 bypass bridge 1.8 m lower
Brick bridge on the double-track embankment; replaced by the bypass bridge
